kind: engineering: per-block activation checkpointing for LM arms that exceed free VRAM (outcome-blind)
note: S2_RB@0.10_s1 hit CUDA OOM at step 0 (3.21 GiB free; RB needs 3.28 GiB with optimizer state). RB was never in the pre-freeze LM benchmark. lm_runner now wraps each block in torch.utils.checkpoint (non-reentrant, RNG state preserved) when arm kind is relaxed_budget or dropkey_budget (E3 DB also OOMs). Probe on random tokens: loss and all gradients bit-identical with and without checkpointing (max |diff| 0), realized TV identical; only memory and wall-clock change. All other arms unchanged. Budget statistics are accumulated during recomputation as well, which scales rows and sums equally and leaves every reported average unchanged.

kind: bug fix: LM DropKey depth schedule (outcome-blind)
note: lm_runner ignored arm.layer_schedule, so LM DK runs used p_max in all six layers. Found from the B11 manipulation record (DK realized D 0.086/0.171/0.343 vs 0.05/0.10/0.20), which shows no outcome. The encoder runner was correct (S1, E-S3, E5 and E4 are unaffected); E3 DB has no schedule. Fix: the factory applies attnreg.depth_schedule as in encoder_runner. Smoke on seed 999: per-layer realized D equals p_max(1-i/6) within 1e-3, pooled 0.100. Remediation: the 3 buggy S2 DK tuning runs, the unopened DK@0.20 sealed files, and the superseded S2 level decision and finals registry were moved to excluded/S2_DK_noschedule. The 3 DK tuning runs are rerun with the same seeds, then the unchanged selection rule is re-applied and the finals are redeclared. S2_AD@0.20_s2 is kept (identical spec, unaffected).

kind: engineering: thermal governor and compute-time budget accounting (outcome-blind; no effect on computation)
note: At the authors request (laptop overheating), thermal_governor.py suspends experiment processes when the GPU reaches 70 C and resumes them at 60 C. Suspension stretches wall time only: seeds, data order, counter-based noise and kernels are unchanged, and no runner logic depends on elapsed time (ThroughputGuard is defined but unused). Each pause is logged in studies/thermal_pauses.jsonl. budget.py computes cap usage as ledger wall time minus the overlap of pauses with each ledgered run, and the drivers fits() now call budget.py, so pauses do not consume the 90 GPU-hour cap. Run records written after this point include pause time in train_seconds; wall-clock cost is reported from the matched benchmark and measure_cost.py, not from run records. Suspend/resume verified on a dummy process.

kind: thermal governor v2: duty cycle (engineering only)
note: v1 pauses lasted ~3 s, because the GPU core cools quickly, so average heat barely fell. v2 adds a duty cycle: after 60 s of work the experiment processes are suspended for at least 60 s and resumed only at <= 60 C. The 70 C ceiling remains. Average GPU power is at most half of full speed and wall time is about 2x or more. The process list is refreshed every 15 s instead of every poll. Pause reasons (duty or thermal) are logged. No effect on computation.

kind: thermal governor v3 (engineering only)
note: the GPU reaches 70 C about 10 s after each resume, so thermal pauses pre-empted the 60 s duty cycle and the GPU worked about 60% of the time. v3: every rest lasts at least as long as the work stretch before it (and until <= 60 C), so the duty cycle is at most 50%. No effect on computation.
